digest.component_or_area: tickets repository rewrite / epoch guard migration
propositions: Execute a one-time force-push to rewrite the tickets branch history, reducing repository size by 92% from 1.04 GiB to ~94 MiB via a pre-computed rewrite script, guarded by operator-confirmed quiescence (zero active sessions, all MCP servers stopped, and no in-flight review-bot work).

Prove deployment readiness and prevent epoch mismatch writer risk through direct runtime proofs: verify the deployed review-bot SHA with a live epoch-mismatch refusal, refresh and probe the host rebar binary with an exact epoch-mismatch refusal, and confirm a completed descendant reconcile-bridge.yml run from the A6-0a merge commit.

Land the identity.enforce_since re-pin (mapped SHA from pre-rewrite state) through normal Gerrit review as a deterministic first post-window write, then validate non-resurrection by confirming old tip is not an ancestor of origin/tickets and that pack growth is under 1 MB.

Re-enable GitHub workflows, AWS timers, and LaunchAgents after post-window reconciliation is validated (green reconcile-bridge run or operator-approved CLI equivalent with zero mutation/recovery failures and canary drift_total=0), then verify rebar fsck is clean and tickets branch is available for sessions.

Validate all 12 acceptance criteria across pre-publication runtime evidence (A6-0a merge, reconcile run, review-bot deployment, host binary refusal), publication correctness (tree match, pack size, commit/merge counts, identity normalized hash), non-resurrection (ancestry and size-pack assertions), and post-enable reconciliation (dry/live/convergence passes, fsck clean with exactly four intentional fork-resolved records).

Revert to the A6-0d bundle and force-with-lease back to the old tip if any pre-push assertion fails or old tip resurfaces post-publication; ensure all consumers are re-converged in forward order and accept that rollback re-diverges already-converged worktrees.
